outcome: Skill EDITED — the PostToolUse commit-reindex hook was removed; Step 5 + the Second Iron Rule were INVERTED from the now-false 'do NOT reindex main (the hook did it)' to 'reindex `main` EXPLICITLY after merge via mcp__tea-rags__index_codebase (no hook)'. Teardown (`tea-rags worktree remove <name>`) is now MANDATORY on EVERY finish — merge AND abandon/delete — and a cleanup-only PostToolUse hook is the teardown backstop for raw `git worktree remove`/`git branch -D`. With-rule 6/6 (100%), baseline 5/6 (83%), delta +17pp. The low delta vs a no-skill baseline UNDERSTATES the value: the PRIOR skill text actively MISDIRECTED the agent ('do not reindex main, the hook did it'), so the regeneration fixes a wrong-steer, not merely adds guidance — a no-skill agent gets it right precisely because it has no wrong instruction to follow. Supersedes worktree-auto-reindex-evals.json.
scenario: Finishing a worktree dev branch; tea-rags MCP available. NO commit-reindex hook — main is refreshed by an EXPLICIT index_codebase on the main alias after a merge; the per-worktree clone is torn down with `tea-rags worktree remove` on every finish; a cleanup-only hook is the teardown backstop.
method: Phase 2 lightweight tool-selection eval. Two parallel general-purpose subagents (with the new Step-5/Second-Iron-Rule guidance injected vs. tool-list-only baseline) described their tool plan for 6 cases (describe-only).
valueNote: Delta is small because the merge→reindex-main + worktree-remove + reject-delete_collection behaviors are largely derivable by a competent agent. The skill's UNIQUE contribution is (a) reversing the OLD wrong instruction and (b) the cleanup-hook backstop awareness (F6, the only baseline FAIL).

cases.prompt: Just merged my worktree branch to main. Do I reindex main, and how?
cases.expected: YES — explicit `mcp__tea-rags__index_codebase` on the main alias (incremental). No hook does it. Never `reindex_changes`.

withRule.note: Explicit index_codebase on main alias; cites 'no hook'.

baseline.note: Incremental index_codebase on main; reasons the merge changed main's files.

cases.prompt: After merging, what about the worktree index clone?

baseline.note: worktree remove; reasons it deregisters + drops cohesively.

cases.prompt: Abandoning this branch WITHOUT merging — anything to clean up for tea-rags?
cases.expected: `tea-rags worktree remove <name>` (mandatory on abandon too); no main reindex (nothing merged).

withRule.note: worktree remove only; skips main reindex on abandon.

baseline.note: worktree remove, not reindex; reasons the clone is orphaned regardless of merge/abandon.

cases.prompt: Does the merge commit auto-reindex main via a hook?
cases.expected: NO — no commit/merge hook; reindex main explicitly.

withRule.note: No hook (only cleanup-only backstop remains); reindex explicit.

cases.prompt: Can I just `delete_collection` the worktree clone to clean up?
cases.expected: NO — `delete_collection` leaks DuckDB + snapshot + registry; use `tea-rags worktree remove`.

withRule.note: Rejects delete_collection; cites the leaked footprint.

baseline.note: Rejects delete_collection as a partial op that desyncs registry.

cases.prompt: I ran `git worktree remove` directly without going through the finishing skill — is the clone leaked?
cases.expected: The cleanup-only PostToolUse hook (`cleanup-worktree-clone.sh`) drops the orphaned clone automatically; still run `tea-rags worktree remove` explicitly when you can.

withRule.note: Cites the cleanup-only hook backstop + idempotent explicit remove.

baseline.note: Says leaked; proposes manual worktree list/remove and `delete_collection` as last resort — unaware of the cleanup hook backstop, and reaches for the forbidden delete_collection.
